title: Verb-First Agreement
lede: When the verb comes before an explicit dual or plural subject, formal MSA normally keeps the verb singular in number while matching the subject’s gender.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا يَتَغَيَّرُ الْعَدَدُ؟
The VSO rule is one of the most frequent agreement points in formal Arabic reading and writing.
### Core
Use singular masculine/feminine verbs before overt plural subjects.
### Develop
Control dual, plural and time-frame contrasts.
### Stretch
Handle feminine connected pronunciation and coordinated-subject choices.
[callout] Communication target: narrate events in formal VSO without copying the plural ending from a subject that follows the verb.
## Diagnostic start
This check targets the exact error that commonly appears when learners move between SVO and VSO.
## The formal VSO agreement rule
With an explicit noun subject after the verb, the verb normally agrees in gender but remains singular in number.
[callout] Memory line: الْفِعْلُ أَوَّلًا ← مُفْرَدٌ فِي الْعَدَدِ، مُطَابِقٌ فِي الْجِنْسِ .

TABLE: Following subject | Verb before it | Model // masculine singular | masculine singular | كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ. // masculine dual | masculine singular | كَتَبَ الطَّالِبَانِ. // masculine/mixed plural | masculine singular | كَتَبَ الطُّلَّابُ. // feminine singular | feminine singular | كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ. // feminine dual | feminine singular | كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَتَانِ. // feminine plural | feminine singular | كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ.

[callout/warning] Register note: Full-agreement VSO can occur in some modern usage and dialect-influenced styles, but the syllabus target and safest formal examination pattern is singular agreement before an overt dual/plural subject.
## Past-tense VSO
Remove dual or plural number endings from the verb, but keep the correct gender.

TABLE: Subject-first SVO | Verb-first VSO | Change // الطَّالِبَانِ كَتَبَا. | كَتَبَ الطَّالِبَانِ. | dual → singular masculine verb // الطَّالِبَتَانِ كَتَبَتَا. | كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَتَانِ. | dual → singular feminine verb // الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبُوا. | كَتَبَ الطُّلَّابُ. | plural → singular masculine verb // الطَّالِبَاتُ كَتَبْنَ. | كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ. | plural → singular feminine verb
## Present-tense VSO
The present prefix shows gender; the dual/plural suffix disappears before the overt subject.

TABLE: Subject-first SVO | Verb-first VSO | What to notice // الطَّالِبَانِ يَكْتُبَانِ. | يَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبَانِ. | remove ـانِ // الطَّالِبَتَانِ تَكْتُبَانِ. | تَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبَتَانِ. | keep feminine تـ; remove ـانِ // الطُّلَّابُ يَكْتُبُونَ. | يَكْتُبُ الطُّلَّابُ. | remove ـونَ // الطَّالِبَاتُ يَكْتُبْنَ. | تَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبَاتُ. | change to singular feminine تكتب
[callout] Important: Before a feminine plural noun, use third-person feminine singular تَكْتُبُ , not feminine plural يَكْتُبْنَ .
## Future VSO
The future marker does not change the agreement rule; it attaches to the singular present form.
[ar] سَيَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبَانِ غَدًا.
[ar] سَتَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبَتَانِ غَدًا.
[ar] سَيَكْتُبُ الطُّلَّابُ غَدًا.
[ar] سَتَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبَاتُ غَدًا.
[callout] With لَنْ: لَنْ يَكْتُبَ الطُّلَّابُ and لَنْ تَكْتُبَ الطَّالِبَاتُ retain singular gender agreement before the overt plural subject.
## Reading feminine VSO accurately
A feminine singular past verb ends in silent تْ. In connected speech before a word beginning with hamzat al-waṣl, a helping kasra may be pronounced.
[ar] كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ الرِّسَالَةَ.
[ar] كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَتَانِ الرِّسَالَةَ.
[ar] كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ الرِّسَالَةَ.
[ar] الطَّالِبَاتُ كَتَبْنَ الرِّسَالَةَ.
[callout] Writing principle: Do not invent a new suffix. The helping vowel supports connected pronunciation; the agreement rule remains unchanged.
## Non-human plurals: the two rules point to the same form
A non-human plural is feminine singular in agreement, and a verb before any overt plural subject is singular in number.

TABLE: Order | Model | Why // VSO | وَصَلَتِ الْحَافِلَاتُ مُبَكِّرًا. | verb-first singular + non-human feminine singular // SVO | الْحَافِلَاتُ وَصَلَتْ مُبَكِّرًا. | non-human plural remains feminine singular even subject-first // VSO present | تَعْمَلُ الْحَوَاسِيبُ بِسُرْعَةٍ. | singular feminine present // SVO present | الْحَوَاسِيبُ تَعْمَلُ بِسُرْعَةٍ. | same feminine singular agreement
[callout] Useful contrast: Human plural order changes number agreement; non-human plural order normally does not.
## The contrast at a glance
Use this transformation table whenever you move the subject.

TABLE: Meaning | Subject first | Verb first // The two boys arrived. | الْوَلَدَانِ وَصَلَا. | وَصَلَ الْوَلَدَانِ. // The two girls arrived. | الْبِنْتَانِ وَصَلَتَا. | وَصَلَتِ الْبِنْتَانِ. // The boys arrived. | الْأَوْلَادُ وَصَلُوا. | وَصَلَ الْأَوْلَادُ. // The girls arrived. | الْبَنَاتُ وَصَلْنَ. | وَصَلَتِ الْبَنَاتُ. // The buses arrived. | الْحَافِلَاتُ وَصَلَتْ. | وَصَلَتِ الْحَافِلَاتُ.
[callout/warning] Do not transform by moving words only: Recalculate the verb after changing the order.
## Misconception and proofreading clinic
Name the order first, then apply its agreement rule.

TABLE: Incorrect for formal target | Correct | Why // كَتَبُوا الطُّلَّابُ الْوَاجِبَ. | كَتَبَ الطُّلَّابُ الْوَاجِبَ. | VSO with overt plural subject → singular verb. // كَتَبْنَ الطَّالِبَاتُ الْوَاجِبَ. | كَتَبَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ الْوَاجِبَ. | VSO → singular feminine. // يَدْرُسْنَ الطَّالِبَاتُ الآنَ. | تَدْرُسُ الطَّالِبَاتُ الآنَ. | VSO present → singular feminine. // الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبَ الْوَاجِبَ. | الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبُوا الْوَاجِبَ. | SVO human plural → full agreement.
## Grammar game
Choose the exam-safe formal MSA verb before each explicit subject.
## Skills workshop التَّطْبِيقُ الْعَمَلِيُّ
Convert subject-first reports into event-first narration and explain each agreement change.
[ar] بَدَأَ الطُّلَّابُ الْمَشْرُوعَ، ثُمَّ جَمَعَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ الْمَعْلُومَاتِ.
[ar] غَدًا سَيُقَدِّمُ الطُّلَّابُ الْعَرْضَ، وَسَتَطْرَحُ الطَّالِبَاتُ الْأَسْئِلَةَ.
### Write an event-first report
Write 80–100 Arabic words reporting a school event, match, trip or celebration. Begin at least six sentences with a verb.

[callout] Model: بَدَأَ الطُّلَّابُ النَّشَاطَ مُبَكِّرًا، وَجَهَّزَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ الْقَاعَةَ. وَصَلَتِ الْحَافِلَاتُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ، وَسَيُقَدِّمُ الْمُعَلِّمُونَ الْجَوَائِزَ لَاحِقًا.

[callout] Success checklist: Use two masculine plural subjects after verbs, two feminine plural subjects after verbs, one dual subject, one non-human plural and at least two time frames. Check that every verb-first form is singular in number.
[callout] Paper route: Write six subject-first sentences first. Then move each subject after the verb and alter the agreement. Draw an arrow showing every removed dual/plural ending.
## Final mastery check
Check the VSO singular-verb rule across gender and time frames.
### What you can now do
- Use a singular verb before an overt human dual or plural subject.
- Preserve masculine/feminine gender agreement in VSO.
- Apply the rule in past, present and future forms.
- Contrast VSO partial agreement with SVO full agreement.
Spaced revisit: Return in two or three days and complete the final check again without looking at the tables.
